## Natural history notes

A small aquatic crambid moth characterized by pale tan to whitish wings with delicate brown markings and a slender, lightly patterned body. In Florida, it is found around ponds, marshes, canals, ditches, lakes, and other freshwater wetlands where floating aquatic plants such as Salvinia, Azolla, and water lettuce occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights near water, while the caterpillars feed on aquatic plants, boring into stems or feeding concealed among floating leaves, and can help suppress dense growth of weedy floating vegetation.
